text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: runtime-1 queue depth spike detected. Error rate up 4x, several customers experiencing 5-10s tail latency. Paging oncall rotation.
oncall-bot: TAGS: runtime, backpressure, customer-impact. Runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/runtime-queue

carter: on it. grabbing current dashboard. which pools are hot?

mira: runtime-1-gpu-pool is saturated, max_inflight=16 currently. avg inflight per-worker = 14, qdepth ~ 1200. incoming RPS steady at 2.8k.

jamal: I see traffic skewed to a few heavy API keys (customer-A, customer-C). Customer-A spikes with long-context generation (samples).

carter: ok we need immediate mitigation to protect overall latency. options: reduce max_inflight on runtime-1, enable shedding for long-running requests, tighten per-key rate limits, or disable non-essential features (reranking). Thoughts?

mira: my vote: soft-shedding + drop max_inflight to 8 for this pool, experiment with 503-on-shed to upstream clients for backlog items. Also temporarily disable rerankers on hosted tier to cut token churn.

jamal: +1. propose sequence: 1) patch max_inflight, 2) set shed action to `reject` for requests >30s waiting, 3) apply per-key soft quota for top offenders (throttle customer-A to 60r/s).

carter: agreed. I'll take step 1 and 2. mira, can you handle per-key throttle? jamal, monitor metrics and customer-facing errors. eva, please draft a customer note if we see impact.

mira: on it. using `redwoodctl` to apply per-key throttle:
```
redwoodctl quotas set --key customer-A --rps 60 --scope hosted
```
I'll also add an override for customer-C if needed.

carter: patching max_inflight now:
```
redwoodctl runtime set --pool runtime-1 --max_inflight 8 --reason "live-shedding to reduce queue depth"
```
Applying in 2m.

oncall-bot: ACTION: max_inflight change deployed by carter at 1758704380.

jamal: seeing immediate reduction in queue length, qdepth down from 1200 -> 340 in 90s. P95 latency dropping from 4.8s -> 1.2s. error rate falling.

mira: quota applied to customer-A. their requests now get 429 bursts, but overall system stabilizing. I also toggled reranker off for hosted: `featureflag.rerank = false` for the runtime-1 route.

eva: drafting customer note for Customer-A and our top 10 tenants: short note explaining temporary throttling to protect system availability, ETA for rolling back 30m.

carter: monitoring. next steps: keep shed in place for 20m, watch sustained qdepth < 200 and error rate < baseline. if stable, gradually raise max_inflight to 12 then 16. log changes in incident tracker.

sre-rotation: acknowledged. logging mitigation steps and assigning follow-up to eng-runtime for postmortem (owner: jamal).

jamal: quick note on telemetry: need a follow-up config to lower per-worker accept window to reduce queueing ingress. will open PR after incident.

mira: agreed — also recommend adding a self-service soft-quota tool so we can throttle noisy API keys without manual `redwoodctl` steps.

carter: thanks team. final status: mitigations applied, system stabilized. switching to monitoring-only. oncall handoff: mira will remain primary for next 30m, then hand back to rotation.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: moved to monitoring state at 1758704741. Please file postmortem if this escalates or customer impact > 5%."
